pr_title: Use templates for issue e-mail subject and body
pr_body:
Fixes #8098 ### Progress (done!) - [x] Add template capabilities. - [x] Add templates that replicate the current mail format for all the replaced templates. - [x] Add more tests. - [x] Add documentation. ### Future enhancements (for other PRs) - [ ] Apply templates to all mail types (activate account, reset password, etc.). - [ ] Support the use of `{{.i18n.Tr}}` for localization, currently tightly coupled to Macaron. ## Updated description This PR adds template capabilities for mails from issues and pull requests. The templates are divided into `issue` and `pull` and will be sought in: ``` templates/mail/issue/default.tmpl templates/mail/issue/new.tmpl templates/mail/issue/comment.tmpl templates/mail/issue/close.tmpl templates/mail/issue/reopen.tmpl templates/mail/pull/default.tmpl templates/mail/pull/new.tmpl templates/mail/pull/comment.tmpl templates/mail/pull/close.tmpl templates/mail/pull/reopen.tmpl ``` If a `pull` template is not found, the corresponding `issue` template is used. If a particular template cannot be found, `default` is used. The template format is as follows: ``` Template for the subject ---------- Template for the body ``` The template for the subject is rendered using `text/template`, while the body of the message is rendered using `html/template`. The dividing line can have any number of dashes greater than three. For example, `issue/comment` could be: ``` {{.SubjectPrefix}}[{{.Repo}}]: @{{.Doer.Name}} commented on #{{.Issue.Index}} - {{.Issue.Title}} ------ {{.Subject}} {{if .IsMention}}

@{{.Doer.Name}} mentioned you:

{{end}}

{{.Body | Str2html}}

---
View it on Gitea.

``` Currently, only `issue/default.tmpl` is present, as that is sufficient to match the current format. The subject part of the template is optional. If absent, a default string is used (current mail subject format). ### Please check [the docs](https://github.com/guillep2k/gitea/blob/fix-email-subject/docs/content/doc/advanced/mail-templates-us.md) for more details. 😄 ----- ## Old PR description (no longer relevant) ~~The idea is to allow some customization for the subject line of notification e-mails. In this PR I've only implemented issue/pr notifications, just to test the waters. More templates can be added in the future (or to this PR, if it is considered incomplete as is).~~ ~~I've added `templates/mail/issue/subject.tmpl`, which looks like this:~~ ``` [{{.Repo}}] {{.Doer}} {{if eq .Action 6}} created issue #{{.Issue.Index}} {{else if eq .Action 7}} created PR #{{.Issue.Index}} {{else if eq .Action 10}} commented on #{{.Issue.Index}} {{else if eq .Action 12}} closed issue #{{.Issue.Index}} {{else if eq .Action 13}} reopened issue #{{.Issue.Index}} {{else if eq .Action 14}} closed PR #{{.Issue.Index}} {{else if eq .Action 15}} reopened PR #{{.Issue.Index}} {{else}} commented/acted upon #{{.Issue.Index}} {{end}} - {{.Issue.Title}} ``` ~~Which produces:~~ ``` [user1/repo1]: user3 commented on #102 - The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog [user1/repo1]: user3 closed issue #102 - The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog [user1/repo1]: user3 created PR #102 - The quick brown fox jumped over the lazy dog ``` ~~Of course a simpler template can be used, one that matches exactly the current behavior for backwards compatiblity.~~ Please let me know your thoughts.
